section.name: Working with the HMVC pattern and Swing

subsection.name: Understanding the HMVC pattern
subsection.p:
First read this article from Javaworld if you have not done it yet: HMVC: The layered pattern for developing strong client tiers
The important points are:
A view is generally a Frame or a panel
Models and controllers are only associated with a frame or a panel
This means that a good HMVC framework forces the user's code to follow the MVC patterns, as opposed to Swing which uses internally a simplified MVC pattern but doesn't provide a clean separation between the MVC parts, and that let the user write some very messy code (if you have been working on a Swing project with no framework guiding developers, you now what I mean...).
The HMVC pattern is used at a higher level of abstraction than in the Swing components: the smallest part is a Panel containing other components, and quite often this panel is the main component in a Frame.
But a higher level of abstraction also means a learning curve and getting used to some practices. The following sections explain how to use Scope in some common cases in GUI development
